source_text:
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοὶ καὶ ἀδελφαί, μετὰ τὸν θεὸν τῆς ἀληθείας ἀναγινώσκω ὑμῖν ἔντευξιν εἰς τὸ προσέχειν τοῖς γεγραμμένοις, ἵνα καὶ ἑαυτοὺς σώσητε καὶ τὸν ἀναγινώσκοντα ἐν ὑμῖν. μισθὸν γὰρ αἰτῶ ὑμᾶς τὸ μετανοῆσαι ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας, σωτηρίαν ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ζωὴν διδόντας. τοῦτο γὰρ ποιήσαντες σκοπὸν πᾶσιν τοῖς νέοις θήσομεν, τοῖς βουλομένοις περὶ τὴν εὐσέβειαν καὶ τὴν χρηστότητα τοῦ θεοῦ φιλοπονεῖν.
καὶ μὴ ἀηδῶς ἔχωμεν καὶ ἀγανακτῶμεν οἱ ἄσοφοι, ὅταν τις ἡμᾶς νουθετῇ καὶ ἐπιστρέφῃ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀδικίας εἰς τὴν δικαιοσύνην. ἐνίοτε γὰρ πονηρὰ πράσσοντες οὐ γινώσκομεν διὰ τὴν διψυχίαν καὶ ἀπιστίαν τὴν ἐνοῦσαν ἐν τοῖς στήθεσιν ἡμῶν, καὶ ἐσκοτίσμεθα τὴν διάνοιαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν τῶν ματαίων.
πράξωμεν οὖν τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ἵνα εἰς τέλος σωθῶμεν. μακάριοι οἱ τούτοις ὑπακούοντες τοῖς προστάγμασιν: κἂν ὀλίγον χρόνον κακοπαθήσωσιν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ, τὸν ἀθάνατον τῆς ἀναστάσεως καρπὸν τρυγήσουσιν.
μὴ οὖν λυπείσθω ὁ εὐσεβής. ἐὰν ἐπὶ τοῖς νῦν χρόνοις ταλαιπωρῇ: μακάριος αὐτὸν ἀναμένει χρόνος: ἐκεῖνος ἄνω μετὰ τῶν πατέρων ἀναβιώσας εὐφρανθήσεται εἰς τὸν ἀλύπητον αἰῶνα.
thought_title: A written appeal for repentance and endurance
orientation: The preacher, having confessed his own sinfulness and fear of judgment, now addresses the congregation directly as brothers and sisters, presenting his written appeal so that they may heed what is written and save themselves.
pass_a_gloss: So then, brothers and sisters, after the God of truth I read to you an appeal, for the purpose of paying attention to the things that have been written, so that you may save both yourselves and the one who reads among you. For I ask of you as a reward that you repent from the whole heart, giving to yourselves salvation and life. For when we have done this, we will set a goal for all the young, for those who wish to labor diligently concerning piety and the kindness of God. And let us not be displeased and let us not be indignant, we who are unwise, whenever someone admonishes us and turns us from unrighteousness to righteousness. For sometimes when we do evil things we do not know it, because of the double-mindedness and unbelief that is in our breasts, and we have been darkened in the mind by the desires of empty things. Let us therefore do righteousness, so that we may be saved to the end. Blessed are those who obey these commandments; even if they suffer hardship for a little time in this world, they will harvest the immortal fruit of the resurrection. Let not the pious person grieve, then, if he suffers hardship in the present times; a blessed time awaits him; that one, having come to life again above with the fathers, will rejoice into the griefless age.

choices.why: The noun denotes a formal petition or intercession; 'appeal' captures the preacher's written plea to the congregation without implying a liturgical prayer.
The phrase is awkward in Greek; 'after the God of truth' preserves the source order and the sense that the reading follows upon or is grounded in the God of truth.
rejected: in the presence of the God of truth

choices.why: The preacher asks for repentance as his recompense; 'reward' keeps the commercial metaphor of μισθός without importing the glossary term ἀντιμισθία.
The dative plural of νέος refers to young people; the preacher wants to set an example for the next generation.
The Greek στήθεσιν is plural and anatomical; 'breasts' preserves the concrete bodily image of the seat of double-mindedness.
ἀλύπητος means 'without grief'; 'griefless age' renders the adjective and noun literally, preserving the eschatological sense of an age free from sorrow.

pass_b_english: So then, brothers and sisters, I read you an appeal in the presence of the God of truth. Pay attention to what is written, so that you may save both yourselves and the one who reads among you. For the reward I ask of you is this: repent with your whole heart, and so give yourselves salvation and life. If we do this, we will set a goal for all the young who wish to labor diligently in devotion and in the kindness of God.

And let us not be displeased and resentful in our foolishness when someone admonishes us and turns us from unrighteousness to righteousness. For sometimes when we are doing evil we do not recognize it, because of the double-mindedness and unbelief that dwell in our breasts, and our understanding is darkened by empty desires.

Let us therefore practice righteousness, so that we may be saved in the end. Blessed are those who obey these commandments. Even if they suffer hardship for a little while in this world, they will harvest the immortal fruit of the resurrection.

So let the devout person not grieve if he suffers misery in the present time. A blessed time awaits him. Coming to life again in the world above with the fathers, he will rejoice in the griefless age.

problems.quote: after the God of truth I read you an appeal to pay attention to what is written
problems.why: 'After the God of truth' is not intelligible English in context.
problems.fix: Likely 'in the presence of God' or 'before God, the God of truth, I read you an appeal.'

problems.quote: coming to life again above with the fathers, he will rejoice in the griefless age
problems.why: 'Above with the fathers' is ambiguous and awkward; reader cannot tell if 'fathers' means patriarchs or church fathers.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'coming to life again in the world above with the fathers' or 'with the patriarchs.'

problems.quote: Brothers and sisters, this is how we ought to think about Jesus Christ
problems.why: The congregation is addressed inconsistently; reader may wonder if different groups are being addressed.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'brothers and sisters' throughout, or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.

edits.old: after the God of truth I read you an appeal
edits.new: in the presence of the God of truth I read you an appeal

edits.old: coming to life again above with the fathers, he will rejoice in the griefless age
edits.new: coming to life again in the world above with the fathers, he will rejoice in the griefless age

fixed: The glossary problem about 'brothers and sisters' is not a real problem in this passage: the English already uses 'brothers and sisters' consistently here.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening appeal by separating the reading and the call to attention, made the requested reward explicit, smoothed sentence rhythm, and clarified the final promise by breaking one long sentence into two.
